title: LED Current-Limiting Resistor Circuit
objective: Verify an LED is wired in series with a current-limiting resistor to a digital output pin, with correct polarity.
safety_notes: Always use a current-limiting resistor (220-330 ohm) with an LED on 5V logic.
Never connect an LED directly across 5V and GND without a resistor.

steps.title: Place LED and resistor
steps.instruction: Insert the LED and a 220 ohm resistor on the breadboard in series.

steps.title: Connect digital output through the resistor
steps.instruction: Connect Arduino D8 to one leg of the resistor.

steps.title: Connect LED with correct polarity
steps.instruction: Connect the resistor's other leg to the LED anode (longer leg), and the LED cathode (shorter leg) to GND.

steps.title: Confirm illumination
steps.instruction: Drive D8 HIGH and confirm the LED lights without excessive current draw.

expected_measurements.description: Safe forward current range for a standard 5mm LED with a 220ohm resistor at 5V.

validation_rules.description: LED and 220 ohm resistor must both be present.
D8 must connect to the resistor, not directly to the LED.
LED anode must face the resistor/supply side; cathode must face GND.
Measured forward current must be in the safe operating range.

troubleshooting.led_not_lighting: LED polarity may be reversed, or the digital pin was never driven HIGH.
troubleshooting.led_dim: Resistor value may be too high, or the pin is not fully HIGH.
troubleshooting.led_very_bright_hot: Resistor may be missing or too low in value — disconnect immediately.
